summary.en: Gold smuggling is now reported to fund an Islamic State-linked insurgency in eastern DRC, with gold moving through Uganda to support rebel groups. An Ebola nurse was killed by a mob and a health worker was wounded while responding to a case, prompting Uganda to tighten its border. The United States imposed sanctions on Rwanda's defence ministry and a military bank for backing M23 rebels and facilitating gold smuggling. The conflict caused 1,158 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Gullsmugling rapporteres nå å finansiere en IS-tilknyttet opprør i Øst-DRC, med gull som går gjennom Uganda for å støtte opprørsgrupper. En ebolasykepleier ble drept av en mobb og en helsearbeider ble såret mens de responderte på en sak, noe som fikk Uganda til å stramme inn grensen. USA innførte sanksjoner mot Rwandas forsvarsdepartement og en militærbank for å støtte M23‑opprørerne og legge til rette for gullsmugling. Konflikten forårsaket 1 158 dødsfall i kamper i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: M23 campaign (2022–present)
background.extract: The M23 campaign is an ongoing series of military offensives launched by the March 23 Movement (M23), a Rwandan-backed rebel paramilitary group in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, since March 2022. In November 2021, M23 first launched attacks against the Congolese military (FARDC) and MONUSCO, seizing military positions in Ndiza, Cyanzu, and Runyoni in North Kivu Province. This coincided with the deployment of Uganda People's Defence Force (UPDF) to the region to combat the Allied Democratic Forces (ADF), a Ugandan rebel group operating in the Congo's North Kivu and Ituri provinces.
